name: BCR-ABL1 KINASE DOMAIN (TKD) MUTATION ANALYSIS [IRMA] BY NGS

data.value:
Test Description:

Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is characterized by the presence of the Philadelphia chromosome, the product of t(9;22)(q34;q11) translocation. This translocation results in BCR-ABL1 fusion protein with constitutive ABL1 tyrosine kinase activity. The kinase inhibitor imatinib (STI571, Gleevec®) inhibits ABL1 kinase activity and is now the standard of care for early phase CML. Prolonged treatment with imatinib can lead to drug resistance, especially in patients with advanced disease. 

A large portion of resistant patients have acquired point mutations in the ABL1 kinase domain that renders the kinase resistant to the drug. Sites of point mutations in ABL1 associated with imatinib resistance span the entire kinase domain but often cluster in important hotspots.(1,2) Total RNA was extracted and nested reverse transcription PCR was performed to detect the BCR-ABL1 transcript and ABL1 kinase domain (KD) region was thereafter sequenced by Next Generation Sequencing for detection of mutant alleles.

Methodology:

Next Generation Sequencing (Massively Parallel Sequencing)

Sample: EDTA Blood

Results and Interpretation:

Test results and Interpretation:  No Mutation Detected

Limitations:

  • Please note that only the variants relevant to the patient’s clinical presentation were reported. A report on all variants present is available upon request, please contact the laboratory.
  • Predisposition to disease may be affected by non genetic factors.
  • This test has not been approved by external accrediting bodies and has been validated according to internal laboratory criteria. Accreditation is not required for the reporting of these test results.
  • For Accurate detection of mutation, at least 1000 BCR-ABL1 Fusion copies/ml should be present in the sample.
  • In cases where the BCR ABL1 load is very low, cases may be released as ‘No Mutation Detected’ with a comment ‘Repeated sequencing revealed no sequenceable Amplicons due to low transcript levels’.
  • All laboratory tests are associated with an error rate of ~1%. These could be due to sample mismatch, inappropriate labeling, processing or technological limitations. Please correlate with clinical features and other investigations for final conclusion and send a repeat sample for analysis if necessary.
  • Rare false positive or negative results may occur due to inherent limitations of the technique involved.
  • Large insertions and deletions may be missed.
  • Mutations having VAF (variant allele frequency) less than 5% are not reported.
  • For test performed on specimens received or collected, it is presumed that the specimen belongs to the patient named or identified as labeled on the container/test request and such verification has been carried out at the point of generation of the said specimen by the sender.
